hypothesis.h0: The lower bound of the Jujutsu-to-Git median read-time ratio remains below 1.05 in every registered repository shape.
hypothesis.h1: At least one registered repository shape establishes Jujutsu machine-readable read overhead of five percent or more against the equivalent Git revision-set read.

falsification: A shape establishes a Jujutsu read-overhead constraint only when its deterministic BCa 95% interval has a lower bound at or above 1.05 and its one-sided bootstrap probability rejects the threshold under Holm-Bonferroni correction across the five-shape family. The constraint blocks claims of latency equivalence and requires latency-sensitive adapter work to retain the Git measurement as its regression control. It does not overturn the independently tested behavioral baseline. The benchmark is repeated only after a documented environment change.

conditions.description: Git machine-readable commit-id log from the colocated fixture repository
Jujutsu machine-readable commit-id log with the working copy ignored

workloads: wide-32: 32 sibling changes sharing one parent
merge-32: two 16-change branches joined by one multi-parent revision
workspaces-8: one history with eight disposable workspaces
population.sampling: paired on each repository shape; condition order is randomized by the registered seed after fixture construction, and fixture construction is outside every timed read

strata.boundary: linear-16 and linear-128 vary only the number of changes
wide-32 and merge-32 vary sibling and multi-parent topology
workspaces-8 varies the number of registered workspaces

effect_size.measure: ratio of paired condition medians (jj-log / git-log)

analysis_plan.uncertainty: deterministic BCa bootstrap 95% ratio interval plus one-sided threshold probability, 10000 resamples, seed 20260831; Holm-Bonferroni across the five registered shapes

exclusion_rule: A measured read is retained in raw measurements and excluded from ratio analysis only when its command exits nonzero, exceeds the registered timeout, or produces no machine-readable stdout. A shape with fewer than 30 successful paired measurements is an invalid cell and the run exits nonzero. Fixture-construction failures are retained in the report and invalidate the run. The rule is applied before the primary metric is inspected and never by judgement.

environment.source_commit: exact source commit recorded by the runner at execution time
toolchains: Jujutsu release from DEFAULT_JJ_VERSION in scripts/bootstrap-jj.sh
Git release recorded by the runner
Python release recorded by the runner

artifacts: --output JSON report containing every warmup and measured raw read
fixture repository manifests with exact JJ and Git source states
per-shape median and BCa ratio summaries
threats: Process startup and filesystem-cache state can dominate short reads; warmups are fixed at 10 and measured reads are run in paired order.
The colocated Git backend may share storage with JJ; the report records both binary identities and exact fixture states.
The benchmark measures machine-readable read commands only; it does not qualify an adapter parser or semantic completion behavior.
Workspace fixture creation is excluded from timing and therefore does not estimate workspace-add latency.
The #33 Atom owns jj-run semantics; this benchmark does not qualify jj-run behavior.
